title: The Distracted Party Guest
setup: You're at a friend's birthday party. You strike up a conversation with someone who keeps glancing at their phone, seeming a little checked-out.
openingLine: Hey, sorry — yeah, hi. It's been a long week, I'm a little fried. Anyway, how do you know Sam?

npcTurns.text: Oh, college roommates, way back. Feels like forever ago. Honestly work has just been swallowing my whole week, I almost didn't come tonight.
It's just been nonstop deadlines, one after another. I keep telling myself it'll slow down but it hasn't yet. What about you, how do you know Sam?
That's a good way to know someone. Honestly I could use a night where I actually put the phone down, I keep checking it out of habit at this point.
Yeah... it's more than habit if I'm being honest, there's a work thing hanging over me tonight. Anyway — sorry, what were you saying?
You know what, thanks for actually asking instead of just letting me disappear into the phone. It's a big presentation Monday I'm dreading.

title: The Tense Work One-on-One
setup: Your manager pulled you aside for an unscheduled one-on-one. Their tone is clipped and something feels off.
openingLine: Thanks for making time. I wanted to talk about the client deck — a couple of things landed wrong in the review yesterday.

npcTurns.text: The numbers on slide four didn't match what finance sent over, and it went out to the client before anyone caught it. I had to do damage control this morning.
I appreciate that. I'm not trying to pile on, I just need to understand what happened so it doesn't happen again. What's your read on where it broke down?
Okay, that's fair, and honestly a second check would've caught it. I was more frustrated because I heard about it from the client before I heard it from you.
That actually matters a lot to me, hearing it directly. I don't need this to be a whole thing, I just needed to know you were on top of it. Are you doing okay otherwise, workload-wise?
Good to know. Let's do a quick check before anything client-facing goes out from now on, just as a habit. Sound fair?

title: Meeting Her Parents for the First Time
setup: You're meeting your partner's mother for the first time, over dinner at her house. She's polite but clearly sizing you up.
openingLine: So. My daughter tells me you two met at work. What is it you do there, exactly?

npcTurns.text: Interesting. And how long have you two been seeing each other now? She doesn't tell me much.
Hm. That's longer than I realized. She's always been private like that, even as a kid — kept things close until she was sure about them.
You'd have liked her at ten years old, she was fearless, climbing everything in sight. Different person these days, more careful. Do you get to see that side of her much?
Good. I worry she's too guarded these days. Anyway — tell me honestly, what do your own parents think of all this?
Fair enough. Well, you've held up better under questioning than the last one did, I'll give you that.

title: "I'm Fine" (She's Not Fine)
setup: You've noticed your friend has been quiet all day. You ask what's wrong and she says she's fine, but her tone says otherwise.
openingLine: I'm fine, really. Just tired I guess.

npcTurns.text: It's nothing, honestly. Just a long week. You don't need to worry about it.
...Okay. It's my mom, actually. Her test results came back and it's not great news. I didn't want to make it a whole thing tonight.
We find out more next week. I keep telling myself it's probably fine but I don't actually know that. I'm scared, honestly.
Thank you for not just letting me say 'I'm fine' and moving on. Most people just take it at face value.
Would you mind just sitting with me for a bit? I don't really want advice, I just don't want to be alone with it right now.

title: The Networking Event Wall
setup: You're at an industry networking event. The person you've approached is giving short, guarded answers and seems hard to draw out.
openingLine: Yeah, I'm in ops. Been doing it a while.

npcTurns.text: A few years now. It's fine.
Honestly these events aren't really my thing. I'm more of a heads-down, get-the-work-done type.
That's actually true, yeah — I built an internal tool last year that cut our reporting time in half. Nobody really asks about that stuff at these things.
It started as just a personal fix for my own headache, honestly, then other people wanted it. What kind of stuff do you work on?
Oh, nice, that's a lot more interesting than what I expected to talk about tonight. Want to grab a coffee sometime and actually compare notes?

title: The Sibling Blowup
setup: A disagreement with your sibling about splitting care for your aging parent has escalated into a heated argument over the phone.
openingLine: You always do this — you disappear for months and then show up acting like you know best about what Mom needs!

npcTurns.text: Easy for you to say, you're not the one driving over there three times a week. I'm exhausted and you're not even here.
I don't want an apology, I want actual help. Do you have any idea what her schedule even looks like right now?
That's the problem — you don't know, because you haven't been asking. She has physical therapy twice a week now on top of everything else.
...Okay. I didn't realize it had gotten to that point. I've been buried at work but that's not really an excuse.
I don't need you to feel guilty, I need you to actually take one of the days. Could you take Tuesdays?
Okay. Thank you. I'm sorry for snapping at you, I've just been carrying this alone for a while.

title: Comforting a Friend After Bad News
setup: Your friend just called to tell you he didn't get the job he'd been counting on for months. He sounds flat and deflated.
openingLine: Yeah, they went with someone else. Guess I wasn't what they wanted.

npcTurns.text: I don't know, man. I really thought this one was it. I'd already kind of pictured my life with it, you know?
The worst part is I have to go back and tell my wife tonight. She was so excited for me, more than I even was.
Yeah. I don't even know what I'm going to say to her. What do you even say after something like this?
That's actually helpful, thank you. I think I've just been trying to figure out how to make it sound less bad than it is.
Would it be weird if I just came over for a bit before I go home? I don't think I want to sit with this alone right now.

title: The First Date Gone Quiet
setup: You're on a first date at a coffee shop. The conversation was flowing at first but has now stalled into an awkward silence.
openingLine: Sorry, I think I just went quiet there for a second. It's not you, I promise, I've just had a weird day.

npcTurns.text: It's nothing crazy, just my roommate situation is a mess right now and it's been on my mind all day.
She's moving out with basically no notice and I have no idea how I'm going to cover rent alone next month.
Sorry, I know this is not exactly first-date material. What about you, is your living situation less of a disaster than mine?
That actually sounds nice, honestly. Okay, I promise I can talk about literally anything other than my rent troubles now.
So — better question. What's something you've been genuinely excited about lately, that has nothing to do with any of this?
